Based on my research, here are the key details about the position of the first Governor-General of India:

## The Position/Role
**Warren Hastings** held the position of **Governor-General of Fort William (Bengal)** from 1773-1785, making him the first Governor-General. This office was created under the Regulating Act of 1773 by the East India Company.

Note: There's an important distinction:
- Warren Hastings was the **first Governor-General of Bengal/Fort William** (1773–1785)
- **Lord William Bentinck** (1834–1835) was the first **Governor-General of All India** after the office was restructured to cover all British territories through the Charter Act of 1833

## Office Location
The Governor-General's office was located in **Calcutta (now Kolkata)**, specifically at **Fort William**. 

- Warren Hastings took his seat as President of the Council at Fort William in April 1772
- Although the appointment was made by the Court of Directors of the East India Company in **London**, the actual administrative work was conducted from Calcutta
- London housed the oversight bodies (Parliament, Court of Directors), while actual governance occurred from Calcutta

## Historical Evolution
- **Before 1858**: Appointed by the East India Company's Court of Directors
- **After 1858**: Title became "Viceroy and Governor-General of India" following the end of Company rule
- **After 1947**: Appointed on advice of independent India's government
- **Abolished**: January 26, 1950, when India adopted its Constitution

So to directly answer your question: the position was physically located in **Calcutta at Fort William**, though appointments were made in London by the East India Company.
